newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telepizza to launch on stock market.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telepizza to launch on stock market.

text.p: Leading Spanish home delivery pizza firm Telepizza is preparing to launch on the stock market and has appointed BBV Interactivos to manage the sale process, the company said in a statement.
Telepizza will put 40 percent of its capital up for sale in a public share offer.
This will be divided into a domestic tranche, with an important part set aside for minority shareholders, and an international tranche exclusively for institutional investors.
"The intention of the company and BBV Interactivos is for shares in Telepizza to be quoted on the Spanish bourse before the end of 1996," it said.
BBV Interactivos will act as global coordinator, while U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch will manage the international tranche of the offer.
Telepizza was founded in 1988 by current chairman Leopoldo Fernandez Pujals.

Profit grew from 155 million pesetas in 1993 to one billion pesetas in 1995. The company made a profit of 707 million in the first half of 1996 and predicts the pace will be maintained until the end of the year.
Telepizza has 218 outlets in Spain and accounts for 55 percent of market share. It employs more than 5,300 people.
